newsitem.title: BRAZIL: EU set to ask for WTO panel on Brazil cars - papers.
newsitem.headline: EU set to ask for WTO panel on Brazil cars - papers.

text.p: The European Union appears set to ask the World Trade Organization (WTO) to create a dispute panel to look into Brazil's automotive regime, Brazilian newspapers reported on Wednesday.

Newspapers said a Brazilian offer to raise its car import quotas for the European Union to 12,000 cars a year from 10,000 and promote slight changes in its car rules was not enough to convince the European Union.

"We are very determined to go ahead with a request for a WTO panel against the automotive regime. I don't say it is 100 percent sure because the decision has not been taken yet. But we concluded that Brazil has limited flexibility to negotiate," an unnamed European Union official was quoted by O Globo daily as saying.
Brazilian and European Union's officials have been meeting in Geneva this week to discuss Brazil's car import policy.
Under Brazil's car industry rules, domestic manufacturers benefit from a preferential 31-percent tariff for car imports whereas manufacturers with no Brazilian production base face a 62 percent tax.
According to O Globo, the European official, who requested anonymity, said the EU wants the Brazilian government to raise the car import quotas to at least 14,500 cars a year.
The newspaper said the European Union should decide whether it will ask for a WTO panel by July 20, when the formal period for a panel request expires, or early September.
